intro

Replying to every customer review takes time, and a templated reply can do more harm than no reply at all. In this video, we walk through Review Reply Copilot, an open source app that drafts replies in your client's voice and keeps a person in charge.
overview

This is the app on first launch. At the top, four tiles track your reviews, your replies, and the time and cost of every step. Below them, three steps take you from an empty project to labeled reviews, so let's go through them in order.
key

Step one connects your Regolo account, and new users can start with a thirty day free trial. Paste your API key in the field, where it stays masked. The app checks it against Regolo's model catalog without running any inference, then saves it in a local dot env file, and the key never travels back to the browser.
key_done
The step closes with a check mark and a short summary, and you can reopen it at any time.
client

Step two brings in the reviews. Each client has a brand profile with its voice, its topics, and the only facts a reply may state. The sample data covers two clients, a software company and an outdoor gear shop, and we'll use the shop, Acme Outdoor.
csv
For your real clients, you import a CSV export from their review tool. The card lists the columns it expects, and the template is one click away. For now, we load the sample reviews.
analyze

Step three sends every review to Clef-Flash, Regolo's decision model. It answers five questions for each one: the sentiment, the topic, whether a person must handle it first, how urgent a reply is, and the language. Eight requests run in parallel, and the bar shows the real progress.
analyze_done
All thirty seven reviews are labeled. The analysis tile shows how long the run took and what it cost, which for this sample is well under one cent.
filters
The reviews now appear with their labels. You can filter by sentiment or topic, or show only the reviews that need a person. Let's open a negative one about a late delivery.
studio

The reply studio shows each label with a confidence bar, and low confidence cases are flagged for a second look. When we click write a draft, a chat model writes the reply with the client's brand rules, and Clef-Flash checks it right away.
checks

Here is the draft, followed by every check. Rule checks cover length, contact details and forbidden phrases. Clef-Flash answers yes or no questions about the text: does it promise compensation, blame the customer, or state something the brand profile doesn't support? If a blocking check fails, the app tries once more, and then asks you to edit.
approve

You can edit the text and run the checks again. When the reply reads well, approve it. The text is copied to your clipboard, and you post it from the review platform yourself, because nothing is published from the app.
escalate

Some reviews should never get an automatic answer. This customer reports that their son was burned by a camping stove, so Clef-Flash marks the review for a person. The draft becomes a neutral holding reply, and it can't be marked as ready.
results
Back at the top, the tiles sum up the session: the reviews analyzed, the replies drafted and approved, and the average time to write a reply.
outro

That's the whole workflow: Clef-Flash decides and checks, a chat model writes, and a person approves. The code is open source, and new Regolo users get a thirty day free trial, so you can try it on your own reviews today.
